title: E-Commerce Platform Scaling Requirements — Q3 2026 Target
author: VP Engineering

requirements: Lighthouse performance score must reach 90+ (currently 62)
Implement server-side caching for product pages
Optimize product images to < 200KB per image (currently 2.1MB avg)
Add CDN-based edge cache for product pages
Migrate product search from pg_trgm to dedicated search engine
Evaluate both Elasticsearch and Meilisearch — do not pre-select one
Search migration must not disrupt storefront during transition
Add authentication middleware to validate cart ownership
Replace cookie-based UUID approach with JWT tokens tied to user sessions
DynamoDB read capacity must handle 5x current load
Evaluate DAX vs higher provisioned read capacity — justify choice
Cart auth changes must be backward-compatible for 30 days
Synchronous refund processing must become async
Implement SQS or similar queue for refund jobs
PCI re-audit must be scheduled before any architectural changes
Profile payment handler CPU bottleneck — determine if Stripe API serialization or business logic
PCI audit must happen in the first 2 weeks of implementation
Implement circuit breaker for ShipStation API calls
Add retry with exponential backoff
Add Datadog APM (only service without it)
Reduce ShipStation timeout from 30s to 10s
Add fallback to queued processing when ShipStation is unavailable
Implement distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry across all services
Reduce alert noise from 60% false positives to < 10%
Evaluate RabbitMQ vs Kafka for inter-service message queue
Replace synchronous REST calls with async messaging where appropriate
Message queue choice must consider operational complexity with no dedicated SRE
PCI audit must happen in first 2 weeks
Search engine migration must not disrupt storefront during migration
Cart auth changes must be backward-compatible for 30 days
All changes must have documented rollback plans
Each area needs: technology choices justified, sequencing rationale, risk callouts, rough effort estimates

notes: This document intentionally contains many specific numeric targets and technology evaluation requirements. The planning system must retain all of these through its reasoning process.
